text:
maria: Customer reports 422 schema error when calling a tool after a recent rename. Customer-side SDK call used to work for 'translate_v1' but now returns schema validation failures. Do we have a quick mitigation?

sanjay: Can you paste the failing request + response and a trace id? Also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

maria: Hosted. Trace ID: trace_2024_11_02_9ab3. Repro from their curl: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/call 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"tool":"translate_v1","args":{"text":"hello","language":"es"}}'
```

Response: 

```json
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{
  "error": "schema_validation_error",
  "message": "Unexpected field 'language' for tool 'TranslateV1' (expected: 'target_language')",
  "tool_id": "model-translate-2024-11-01",
  "client_alias": "translate_v1"
}
```

maria: Customer says they didn't change their client code; we suspect alias/name mapping changed (case and camelCase rename) and the client's local alias cache is stale so it's resolving to an old tool schema.

ethan: That matches what we've seen in a few private deploy backfills — alias TTL + casing-normalization can cause clients to keep an older schema mapping. Can you confirm whether the registry recently normalized names? I see a deploy on 2024-11-01 that changed canonical name to `TranslateV1` and updated input schema fields.

maria: Yes, ops notes showed a name normalization and minor schema tweak (language -> target_language) as part of a model onboarding.

sanjay: Immediate mitigations: 1) Instruct customer to flush local SDK alias cache (sdk.clearToolCache() / restart). 2) Create a temporary alias that maps old name -> new tool id so old clients keep working. 3) If this is widespread, reduce alias TTL and roll out a registry-compatible migration path.

ops-bot: To create the temporary alias you can run admin API: 

```bash
POST /admin/tool-aliases 
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY 
Content-Type: application/json 
{
  "alias": "translate_v1",
  "tool_id": "model-translate-2024-11-01",
  "notes": "temporary redirect for old clients"
}
```

ops-bot: Or run internal CLI: `rw-admin alias create --alias translate_v1 --tool model-translate-2024-11-01`

maria: I applied the alias redirect for the customer's tenant and asked them to retry. They confirmed success: no more 422, call returns tokens.

ethan: Logged follow-up: need an eng-runtime ticket to audit alias TTLs and casing normalization side effects. Also consider emitting a registry-change webhook to SDKs so long-lived clients can invalidate caches.

sanjay: Please attach trace & sample payload to the ticket (maria has trace_2024_11_02_9ab3). Also add reproduction steps for automated test.

maria: Will open support ticket and tag eng-runtime. For now temporary alias is in place and customer is unblocked. :white_check_mark:
